title: Generative model
bullets: Conditional diffusion model (4.0M parameters) and VAE trained on the Jetson from 13,076 real frames, whole trials held out
Diffusion training: 53 min, ~18.5 W, ~59 kJ (16 Wh); held-out loss still falling, so undertrained
HT matches real in occupied scenes (two people 0.1038 vs 0.1040); empty room 17% low
Pixel noise is 60–75% of real (52–77 vs 79–116 mK); VAE is 5–10× too smooth
YOLO finds the single person in 8–16% of generated frames vs 80–100% real
Cannot produce a lamp without a person, and has no fog or crowd data
Sampling: 23 frames/s at 10 steps, 4.6 at 50 steps
Verdict: in-distribution A0/A1-like frames only; no nearest-neighbour sign of memorisation
notes: results/thermal-generative/metric_table.md, logs/, harness_runs.csv. Single seed, 6 held-out trials, 2 harness repeats. Checkpoints are on the Jetson only.

title: Thermal-trained YOLO
bullets: YOLOv8n fine-tuned on FLIR thermal driving images (9,306 images, 16 of 20 epochs) vs stock COCO YOLOv8n
On FLIR test images it is far better: person mAP50 0.84 vs 0.52, recall 0.78 vs 0.50
On real Lepton recordings it is worse: person found in 71% of one-person frames vs 90% for stock
One bank: calls the person a car in 70% of frames (person 6% vs 99% stock); top confidence 0.46 vs 0.70
Neither model false-alarms in any empty-room bank
Inference 1.36 ms faster (29.49 vs 30.85 ms): 4-class head instead of 80; still flat across scenes
Paced pipeline -1.28 ms (CI -1.61 to -0.96), -0.072 W, -8.3 mJ per frame; post-processing unchanged on average
Overnight conclusion holds for both models: cost follows detections, not entropy
notes: docs/thermal-yolo.md; results/thermal-yolo/. FLIR ADAS is outdoor driving footage, so this is not a model trained on the test room. One seed, one paced round per model, no ground-truth boxes on Lepton frames. Added the morning of 24 Nov.
